source.how: ASC 5 lists six requirements that 'apply in the Park Blocks ASC'. Items 1-3 and 6 lay out streets, blocks, the median and a pedestrian accessway, which a pod on an existing lot does not change. Two reach a lot: item 4, no vehicle access from the Park Blocks to residential property adjacent to them, and item 5, no parking lot between the street and the adjacent buildings. This file holds the lots inside the ASC 5 outline (at least 90 percent of the lot) on which either can bind the pod, whole, and, at their share inside, the lots the outline cuts. Item 4: a lot within 60 ft of one of the three Park Blocks median tracts (taxlots 1N117BC00600, 1N117BD00800, 1N117BD00900: 100 ft wide rectangles on one east-west line, the 100 ft median of item 3, 34 ft from the lots facing them across the 35 ft couplet right-of-way), or one the Special Setbacks Map marks as fronting a Park Blocks stroke. The screen cannot bar a driveway from one named street, so such a lot is held. Item 5: the pod parks in a court behind the building (no side court is offered in these districts: parking_side_prohibited is unread), which on an interior or corner lot stands behind the building and not between it and a street. Only a lot with street right-of-way along two opposite sides puts that court between a street and the building, so such a lot is held: a side of the lot's minimum rotated rectangle is on right-of-way when more than 60 percent of a strip 2 to 10 ft outside its middle 60 percent lies outside every taxlot. An alley that is right-of-way rather than a tract counts as a street here, which can only hold a lot that need not be. The three median tracts are held too. Every other lot inside ASC 5 is outside this file, so its own district standards answer it.
